A robot is granted a dock lease at a station only while that station is below its capacity; the grant starts a time-to-live countdown and consumes one capacity unit. A robot may renew its active lease to reset the time-to-live. As time passes an active lease ticks down, and once it reaches zero the lease expires and is reclaimed, freeing the robot's dock and returning a capacity unit to its station. There is also a privileged admin override: while unlocked, an administrator may force-reclaim a robot's lease regardless of its time-to-live, likewise returning the capacity unit. The override lock can be toggled on or off. SAFETY PROPERTY: no charging station ever holds more active dock leases than its capacity allows.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od13m8p1t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Operators, Machines

VARIABLES coarse, fine, pending, committed, record
\* coarse: holder of the coarse region-controller lock, or "none"
\* fine: [Machines -> Operators \cup {"none"}] holder of each fine per-machine lock
\* pending: order-free set of inventory updates awaiting application (reorderable)
\* committed: updates the system has declared committed
\* record: updates durably written into the shared inventory record
vars == <<coarse, fine, pending, committed, record>>

Updates == Machines
MachineOf(u) == u

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Operators \cup {"none"}
  /\ fine \in [Machines -> Operators \cup {"none"}]
  /\ pending \subseteq Updates
  /\ committed \subseteq Updates
  /\ record \subseteq Updates

Init ==
  /\ coarse = "none"
  /\ fine = [m \in Machines |-> "none"]
  /\ pending = Updates
  /\ committed = {}
  /\ record = {}

\* Acquire the coarse region-controller lock first
AcquireCoarse(o) ==
  /\ coarse = "none"
  /\ coarse' = o
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, pending, committed, record>>

\* Acquire a fine per-machine lock, only while holding the coarse lock
AcquireFine(o, m) ==
  /\ coarse = o
  /\ fine[m] = "none"
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![m] = o]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, pending, committed, record>>

\* Apply any pending update (any order -> reordering) while holding both locks: mark it committed
\* AND durably write the shared record together, then release the fine and coarse locks
Commit(o, u) ==
  /\ u \in pending
  /\ coarse = o
  /\ fine[MachineOf(u)] = o
  /\ committed' = committed \cup {u}
  /\ record' = record \cup {u}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {u}
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![MachineOf(u)] = "none"]
  /\ coarse' = "none"

\* An operator may back off, releasing whatever locks it holds, and retry later
Release(o) ==
  /\ (coarse = o \/ \E m \in Machines : fine[m] = o)
  /\ coarse' = IF coarse = o THEN "none" ELSE coarse
  /\ fine' = [m \in Machines |-> IF fine[m] = o THEN "none" ELSE fine[m]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, committed, record>>

Next ==
  \/ \E o \in Operators : AcquireCoarse(o) \/ Release(o)
  \/ \E o \in Operators, m \in Machines : AcquireFine(o, m)
  \/ \E o \in Operators, u \in Updates : Commit(o, u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed inventory update is durably present in the shared record: no update is lost.
NoLostUpdate == committed \subseteq record

=============================================================================
nl: A vending machine network applies inventory updates under hierarchical locks: an operator must first take the coarse region-controller lock and only then a fine per-machine lock on the machine an update targets. Pending inventory updates form an order-free set, so an operator may apply any of them in any order (messages can be reordered). Applying an update is done while holding both locks: it marks the update committed and, in the same step, durably writes it into the shared inventory record, then releases both the fine and coarse locks. An operator that cannot make progress may back off, releasing whatever locks it holds, and retry later. SAFETY PROPERTY: every inventory update that has been committed is always durably present in the shared inventory record, so no update is ever lost.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od2m4p4t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Robots, Tasks, Bays, QCap, BayCap
ASSUME QCap \in Nat /\ BayCap \in Nat

VARIABLES pending, queue, occ, at
\* pending: tasks not yet admitted to the dispatch queue
\* queue: order-free set of admitted tasks awaiting a robot (bounded by QCap, backpressure)
\* occ: [Bays -> 0..Card(Robots)] number of robots currently inside each loading bay
\* at: [Robots -> Bays \cup {"none"}] which bay a robot is currently in
vars == <<pending, queue, occ, at>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ pending \subseteq Tasks
  /\ queue \subseteq Tasks
  /\ occ \in [Bays -> 0..Cardinality(Robots)]
  /\ at \in [Robots -> Bays \cup {"none"}]

Init ==
  /\ pending = Tasks
  /\ queue = {}
  /\ occ = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
  /\ at = [r \in Robots |-> "none"]

\* Admit a pending task into the dispatch queue; backpressure blocks admission when full
Admit(t) ==
  /\ t \in pending
  /\ Cardinality(queue) < QCap
  /\ pending' = pending \ {t}
  /\ queue' = queue \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, at>>

\* An idle robot claims any queued task (any order -> reordering) and returns the task to pending
Claim(r, t) ==
  /\ at[r] = "none"
  /\ t \in queue
  /\ queue' = queue \ {t}
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, at>>

\* A robot enters a loading bay only if the bay is below its capacity
EnterBay(r, b) ==
  /\ at[r] = "none"
  /\ occ[b] < BayCap
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = occ[b] + 1]
  /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![r] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queue>>

\* A robot leaves its bay, freeing a slot
LeaveBay(r) ==
  /\ at[r] # "none"
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![at[r]] = occ[at[r]] - 1]
  /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![r] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queue>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Tasks : Admit(t)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, t \in Tasks : Claim(r, t)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays : EnterBay(r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : LeaveBay(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No loading bay ever holds more robots than its capacity.
CapacityOK == \A b \in Bays : occ[b] <= BayCap

=============================================================================
nl: A warehouse robot fleet pulls jobs through a bounded dispatch queue with backpressure. Tasks start in a pending pool and are admitted into the dispatch queue only while it has room; when the queue is full, admission is blocked rather than dropping the task. The queue is order-free, so an idle robot may claim any queued task in any order, returning the task to the pending pool as it services it (messages can be reordered). Independently, an idle robot may enter one of the loading bays, but only when that bay is below its capacity, and it later leaves the bay to free a slot. SAFETY PROPERTY: no loading bay ever holds more robots than its capacity allows.
